newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst reorganises CR&T research, technology unit.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst reorganises CR&T research, technology unit.

text.p: German chemicals giant Hoechst AG said on Wednesday that it plans to establish its Corporate Research & Technology (CR&T) unit as an automonous technology unit at the beginning of 1998.
The move comes as part of Hoechst's stated aim of restructuring into a strategic management holding company, the group said in a statement.
"The mission of this unit will remain unchanged: to identify, assess and develop new technologies that can be of strategic importance to the entire Hoechst group," Hoechst said.
As part of the move, Hoechst will shut down all operative research and business assessment and planning activities at Corpus Christi, Texas by the end of the year.
Some functions from Corpus Christi will be moved to CR&T's Frankfurt and/or a Hoechst business unit.
CR&T's operations in Charlotte, North Carolina will be shut down at the end of June and consolidated into its Summit, New Jersey organisation, where appropriate.
Around 230 employees will be affected by the changes initially and around 315 jobs will go by the year 2000.
